title: Landing voice: edge anchors & hero experiment pack
body:
Objective:
Small, testable set of hero and subhead variants that lean into two adjacent truths: (1) engineering-first teams need predictable inference economics, and (2) reliability/fallbacks are often the untold feature that keeps apps in production. Build 6 compact variants (hero + subhead + micro-CTA) that we can A/B on top funnel and measure conversion to quickstart and try-for-free.

Context / working constraints:
- Primary audience: backend/ML engineers evaluating an inference platform for production (latency-sensitive, cost-conscious). Secondary: platform/infra leads who buy Dedicated/Private.
- Messaging must map to tangible proof hooks (latency p95, $/1K tokens, fallback tiers). Avoid vague "best" claims.
- Keep tone technical but approachable — short noun-verb headlines, developer-oriented benefit second.
- We have product proof points: routing/fallbacks, prefix caching, per-route cost breakdowns, dedicated pools. Use them.
- Timeline: lightweight experiments to ship in 2 sprints (copy -> A/B variants -> telemetry).

Hero variants (6 compact options) — each line = [hero] // [subhead] // [micro-CTA]
1) "Control inference costs without rewrites" // "Route, cache, and quantize per-route — predictable latency and spend" // "See cost examples"
2) "Keep your app live when models fail" // "Automatic fallback and region routing to avoid outage windows" // "Read fallback flow"
3) "Same API. Multiple SLAs." // "Hosted, Dedicated, or Private — pick latency and isolation you need" // "Compare modes"
4) "Get predictable latency at scale" // "GPU-optimized runtime with KV caching and continuous batching" // "Performance benchmarks"
5) "Optimize token spend, preserve quality" // "Smart batching + quantization recipes tuned per workload" // "Try Optimize"
6) "One runtime for all your inference risks" // "Graceful degradation, traces, and rollback-aware rollouts" // "Explore rollouts"

Microcopy and scaffold notes (for product pages and feature callouts):
- Short bullets under hero (3 bullets):
  • "Per-route cost & latency breakdowns — identify hot prompts in minutes"
  • "Automatic model fallbacks & cross-region routing — reduce outage blast radius"
  • "Dedicated GPU pools and private control plane for regulated workloads"
- CTA taxonomy: "Try free" (top), "Compare modes" (product buyers), "Docs: routing & caching" (engineers), "Contact Sales" (enterprise interest).
- Micro-CTAs should map to events: view-quickstart, open-compare-table, open-routing-doc, demo-request. Add tracking hooks in GH PR.

Product page copy skeleton (short form to populate):
Headline: "Inference that survives production"
Subhead: "Predictable latency, transparent costs, and operational controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
Three feature tiles (title / 1-line benefit / proof):
 - "Smart routing" / "Route by latency, cost, or region; automatic fallback when variants disagree" / "p95 latency drop; fallback metric"
 - "Cost controls" / "Per-route budgets, batching suggestions, and detailed token breakdowns" / "example $/1M token comparisons vs baseline"
 - "Operational guardrails" / "Canary rollouts, traceable prompts, and audit logs for compliance" / "SLA/uptime targets per tier"

Competitive notes (quick and dirty):
- Major clouds (Managed Endpoints): strong on ecosystem and infra breadth, weaker on specialized inference economics and fallback policies. Their pitch = "one-stop infra". Our counter: "economics and graceful degradation for real LLM workloads."
- Pure LLM APIs: easy dev experience, but opaque cost and limited operational controls. Pitch = "simplicity". Our counter: "same simplicity + predictable unit economics + ops hooks."
- Self-hosted inference vendors: deep runtime control but heavy ops lift. Pitch = "you control everything". Our counter: "give you control where it matters (dedicated/private + config) without building the runtime and rollout plumbing."
Open competitive claims to test on page: "cheaper at 90%ile latency for chat flows" (need benchmark link), "smaller outage windows with automatic fallback" (we have internal test harness).

Objections & rebuttals (copy-ready lines):
- "We can manage on VMs ourselves" → "Sure — many customers do — but we cut weeks of ops work and provide guardrails (rollouts, KV caching, traceable prompts) you’d otherwise implement ad-hoc."
- "Tokens are unpredictable" → "We show per-route spend and provide batching/cache suggestions tied to real requests, not just theoretical guidance."
- "Vendor lock-in concerns" → "Same API across hosted/dedicated/private; pin model versions and export logs — migration paths are explicit."

Experiment plan & success metrics:
- Experiment: test variant 1 vs variant 4 vs baseline hero (existing) on homepage for 3 weeks.
- Primary metric: click-through to quickstart (conversion uplift target: +18% relative).
- Secondary metrics: demo-requests, docs opens for routing & caching, bounce rate on hero scroll.
- Qual: collect short intercept survey for visitors who clicked (one-question: "Main reason for visiting today?") to ensure signal quality.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need up-to-date numbers for $/1M token comparisons (product to provide). Owner: Ravi. Due: 2025-09-22.
- Benchmark artifacts for fallback tests — link / short reproducible harness. Owner: Claire. Due: 2025-09-25.
- Engineering: add event hooks in site GH-PR so we can capture view-quickstart & compare-modes. Owner: Marco.

Notes to self (informal):
- Avoid overusing "trust" and "reliability" as they feel empty without numbers — lead with specific mechanics (fallbacks, routing, caching).
- Try a variant that anthropomorphizes infra risk (e.g., "When models misbehave, your app should not"), but keep tests focused — cultural risk of sounding alarmist.

Appendix (quick copy snippets for A/B insertion):
- Variant micro-CTA examples: "See cost examples" / "Read fallback flow" / "Performance benchmarks" / "Try Optimize" / "Compare modes" / "Explore rollouts"
- Short feature bullets for product list pages (to reuse across site):
  • "Per-request traces and prompt attribution."
  • "Autoscaling with predictable tail latency."
  • "KV prefix caching to avoid re-generation costs."
  • "Dedicated pools with capacity reservation and burst lanes."

Status: draft -> ready for small review.
Next steps: iterate with product to fill numeric proof points, then push GH-PR for site variant + telemetry.

Last edited by Aisha Patel — quick check with Ravi on numbers before ship.
